context: The head nodes in the left column represent vertices. Arrows pointing right in each row are references in a linked list of neighbors. They do not indicate directed edges in the original graph. At each step, the table gives the complete neighbor lists in the order shown. A vertex retains its identity even if its row changes position.
description: An undirected edge appears in both endpoints' lists, so adding or removing an edge requires updating both rows. To add an isolated vertex, add an empty list. To remove a vertex, remove its entire row and scan the remaining lists to delete entries for that vertex.

The figure inserts each new neighbor at the head of the list. The lists earlier in the text and the code append new neighbors at the end (the code uses dynamic arrays in place of linked lists). Both orders represent the same undirected connections.

frames.announcement: Initially, the vertices are [1, 3, 2, 5, 4], with 6 edges. The neighbors of 1 are 3 and 5. There is no edge 1—2 yet.
frames.explanation: The vertices are initially ordered [1, 3, 2, 5, 4]. There are 6 undirected edges: 1—3, 1—5, 2—3, 2—5, 2—4, and 4—5. There is no edge 1—2 yet. Each table row lists the neighbors of one vertex.
frames.key_state: Initially, the vertices are [1, 3, 2, 5, 4], with 6 edges. The neighbors of 1 are 3 and 5. There is no edge 1—2 yet.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency list, step 1: complete initial state

frames.title: Initialize the five-vertex graph

frames.announcement: Put each of vertices 1 and 2 at the head of the other's list to add undirected edge 1—2. There are now 7 edges.
frames.explanation: Add undirected edge 1—2 by inserting 2 at the head of the list for vertex 1 and 1 at the head of the list for vertex 2. The other rows stay the same. There are still 5 vertices, and the edge count rises to 7. The table gives both updated lists in full.
frames.key_state: After adding 1—2, the vertices are [1, 3, 2, 5, 4], with 7 edges. The neighbors of 1 are 2, 3, and 5. The neighbors of 2 are 1, 3, 5, and 4.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency list, step 2: complete state after adding edge 1—2

frames.title: Add edge 1—2

frames.announcement: Remove each of vertices 1 and 3 from the other's list to delete edge 1—3. There are now 6 edges, and 3 is connected only to 2.
frames.explanation: Remove undirected edge 1—3 by deleting 3 from the list for vertex 1 and 1 from the list for vertex 3. The graph still has 5 vertices and now has 6 edges. The neighbors of 1 are 2 and 5, and 3 is connected only to 2.
frames.key_state: After removing 1—3, the vertices are [1, 3, 2, 5, 4], with 6 edges. The neighbors of 1 are 2 and 5, and 3 is connected only to 2.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency list, step 3: complete state after removing edge 1—3

frames.title: Remove edge 1—3

frames.announcement: Append an empty list for vertex 6. There are now 6 vertices and 6 edges.
frames.explanation: Append an empty list for vertex 6. The rows are now ordered [1, 3, 2, 5, 4, 6]. All other rows stay the same. There are still 6 edges, and vertex 6 is isolated.
frames.key_state: After adding isolated vertex 6, the vertices are [1, 3, 2, 5, 4, 6], with 6 edges. The list for 6 is empty, and 3 is connected only to 2.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency list, step 4: complete state after adding isolated vertex 6

frames.title: Add isolated vertex 6

frames.announcement: Remove the entire row for vertex 3 and delete 3 from the list for vertex 2, its only remaining neighbor. The remaining vertices keep their names: [1, 2, 5, 4, 6]. Vertex 6 is still isolated, and there are 5 edges.
frames.explanation: Remove the entire row for vertex 3, then scan the remaining lists for entries pointing to 3. Edge 1—3 was removed in step 3, so only vertex 2 is still connected to 3. Delete 3 from its list. The remaining vertices are ordered [1, 2, 5, 4, 6]. Moving rows up does not rename the vertices. The neighbors of 2 are 1, 5, and 4. Vertex 6 is still isolated, and there are 5 edges.
frames.key_state: After removing vertex 3, the vertices are [1, 2, 5, 4, 6], with 5 edges. Vertex 2 keeps its name, and its neighbors are 1, 5, and 4. Vertex 6 has no neighbors.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency list, step 5: complete state after removing vertex 3

frames.title: Remove vertex 3

summary: Follow changes to the rows and their neighbors as edges and vertices are added to or removed from an adjacency list.
title: Adding and removing edges and vertices in an adjacency list
